basis: Axonal peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent pes cavus in 14/18 supports skeletal involvement. Scoliosis occurs in only 3/18.
Congenital partial absence of the pericardium; possible cardiac herniation remains within the cardiovascular axis.
Vertebral skeletal dysplasia with short-trunk stature and platyspondyly. Mild corneal opacities lack established functional impairment; a metabolic enzyme defect is not firmly established.
Endocardial fibrosis causes cardiomyopathy and cardiac insufficiency. The supplied syndromic HPO profile is discordant with isolated endocardial fibroelastosis.
Congenital abnormal cranial nerve innervation produces defining eyelid synkinesis and ptosis; other systemic abnormalities are uncommon.
Lesion of a peripheral nerve; ancestors and named subtypes establish peripheral nervous system disease.
Glycosylation disorder with immunodeficiency. Liver dysfunction and cutis laxa each occur in 3/3; immunoglobulin and CD4 deficiencies support the immune mechanism.
Defined by myocardial hypertrophy, sometimes with ventricular outflow obstruction; extracardiac syndromic features do not apply across this umbrella.
Neoplasm originates in arteries or veins; other organ sites depend on the subtype.
The familial obstructive jaundice of infancy parent supports an inherited hepatobiliary disorder. Nonhemolytic jaundice does not establish blood disease.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; anosmia in 8/8 establishes olfactory dysfunction and hearing impairment occurs in 6/8. Dental anomalies affect only 2/8.
Acetaminophen poisoning principally targets the liver through toxic hepatocellular necrosis. Renal injury is a minority complication.
Ulceration confined to the vulva is a female reproductive organ disorder; no infectious or systemic cause is specified.
Persistent inflammation of the bile ducts. Chronic inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Malignant neoplasm of the spinal meninges, a central nervous system site.
Hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy with optic atrophy defines this disease group; the optic nerve is assigned to the ocular axis.
Neurodevelopmental degeneration and visual dysfunction define the syndrome. Scoliosis occurs in 5/7 and gingival overgrowth in 4/7; retinal electrophysiology is abnormal in 3/6.
Galloway-Mowat syndrome combines neurodevelopmental disease with glomerular disease; proteinuria occurs in 6/12. Optic atrophy affects 13/14.
Endocrine, olfactory and cardiac defects define the syndrome. Renal agenesis occurs in 30-79%; hearing loss and cleft palate also occur in 30-79% but are omitted at the cap.
Skeletal thoracic dysplasia; anal atresia 2/2, cardiac defects at least 1/2. Pulmonary hypoplasia is a major thoracic phenotype; subtype-specific renal disease is not established.
Congenital central hypothyroidism with low free T4 and inappropriately normal TSH; thyroid hypoplasia occurs in 9/17. No common additional organ damage is established.
Bacterial infection of beard or mustache hair follicles, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
Childhood mixed germ cell malignancy arising in the testis, a reproductive site; an endocrine gland disorder is not established.
Childhood embryonal carcinoma arising in ovarian germ cells; reproductive tumour origin alone does not establish endocrine disease.

Inherited hepatobiliary bile-acid handling disorder; characteristic fat malabsorption and steatorrhea establish common digestive dysfunction. Rickets frequency is uncertain; pruritus alone is excluded.
